source.title: 诊断学（第10版）
source.section: 第五篇 辅助检查 第一章 心电图 第六节

textbook_summary: Premature ectopic P-prime waves differ in morphology from sinus P waves.
The normally conducted example has P-prime-to-R > 120 ms and narrow QRS complexes.
The pause is usually incompletely compensatory: the interval between surrounding sinus P waves is less than twice the normal PP interval.
A blocked premature atrial P-prime wave may overlap the preceding T wave without a subsequent new QRS-T complex (figure C).
Premature atrial beats may show intraventricular aberrancy with broad abnormal QRS complexes, often resembling RBBB (figure B); not all sinus beats must be broad.

authored_choices.pPrimeShape: Reuses the normalized rounded P table with 80 ms duration and explicit electrode amplitudes, inverted in II/III/aVF and positive in aVR. No specific ectopic focus is localized.

blockedVariant.pPrimeOverlay: P-prime spans 2000-2080 ms and naturally overlaps the preceding T at 1940-2080 ms; the existing T wave is not replaced.
blockedVariant.unchanged: The 3100 ms group, P/P-prime amplitudes and durations, QRS/QT/T and 80 ms atrial mechanical delay match the normally conducted example. Only ventricular electrical/mechanical events corresponding to the premature atrial beat are suppressed.
blockedVariant.pulseSupport: Standard Pleth/ABP/PA support of 512/600/640 ms is retained because the minimum RR is 800 ms.

aberrantVariant.morphology: Reuses complete RBBB electrode tables and secondary ST/T only for ventricular beats whose original ordinal modulo 4 equals 3.
aberrantVariant.unchanged: The normally conducted example retains P/P-prime, PR 160 ms, coupling 500 ms, pause 1000 ms, mechanical timing, pressure and other physiological channels. Durations are authored choices.

implementation: Normal and ectopic P use distinct event kinds. The sinus grid resets after the premature atrial beat according to the selected pause. Periodic repetition is not a random incidence model.
Direct beat indexing and exact half-open interval counts; the timeline and pressure use the same mechanical-event accessor.
Short-term recovery reconstructs bounded lookback without replaying from the epoch or indirectly producing premature atrial beats through temporary heart-rate changes.
The conducted mode has minimum PP/RR of 500 ms. The blocked mode separately bounds minimum PP at 400 ms and RR at 800 ms. Sinus QRS/T remain unchanged.
Twelve-lead and monitor lead II share one source. Both demos load fixed examples and clear previous rhythm/morphology settings.

Blocked PAC still emits PrematureAtrialElectrical and AtrialMechanical. The shared indexed accessor excludes both VentricularElectrical and VentricularMechanical in the final slot. No new PR measurement or sinus-arrest inference is added.

VentricularCycles is an immutable 1-64-slot mask restricted to VentricularElectrical. Sinus and aberrant bands are selected exclusively, without duplicate events. Recovery retains the original ordinal; the QRS measurement summary explicitly measures sinus slot 0 only.
limitations: Intervals, QT, the P-prime electrode vector and one premature atrial beat after every three sinus beats are authored choices, not traced textbook recordings or calibrated electrophysiological parameters.

Only one fixed RBBB aberrancy example is covered. Other ectopic P-prime shapes, coupling/PR prolongation and aberrant morphologies are unimplemented; no refractory period or automatic Ashman phenomenon is inferred.

Mechanical events occur early, but CVP/Pleth/ejection inputs retain existing shapes and amplitudes without beatwise filling/stroke-volume feedback. Ventricular mechanical events may be explicitly disabled.
No automatic diagnosis or RR/QTc detection; fixed QT does not adapt to short/long intervals.
Other rhythms, including PVC/PJC/VT, and other physiological waveform gaps remain open.
Windows visual behavior is not yet manually verified.
